To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The failure of the livestock sector to generate economic benefits for the majority of smallholders in Ethiopia is due to weak innovation systems functions such that entrepreneurship, knowledge diffusion and policy advocacy.
the low uptake of agricultural technology and economic opportunities in smallholder livestock sector is due to weak or missing functions of the innovation system.

The failure of the smallholder livestock farmers in Ethiopia to adopt improved technologies has been due to a combination of economic, social and political processes that are embedded in the innovation systems framework.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of missing links in the livestock sector and the need for innovative business models that facilitate the uptake of technologies.

the role of the innovation system framework as a tool for identifying missing links in the adoption and diffusion of improved technologies and commercialization opportunities in livestock value chains.
the missing links in technology and knowledge systems that are critical for the development of livestock value chains in Ethiopia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the livestock innovation systems in Ethiopia are weak, and that this is a major reason for the slow pace of technology adoption and commercialization of smallholder livestock production.
there is a need for a holistic and integrated approach to livestock sector development that can address the missing links in innovation systems.

the adoption of improved technologies in Ethiopia is not only a technical issue but it is also an issue of the functioning of innovation system in livestock value chains and its ability to facilitate the coordination of the various actors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adoption of new technologies and commercialization in livestock production systems is a complex process that requires a multi-disciplinary approach that takes into consideration the social, political, and economic context of the system.
the livestock sector in Ethiopia has been characterized by weak innovation systems functions.
the livestock sector in Ethiopia is still at an early stage of innovation and technology adoption, which is reflected by the low uptake of technologies and low productivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the innovation system approach can be a useful framework for understanding the dynamics of technology uptake and commercialization of livestock production systems.
there is a need to strengthen the functions of innovation systems in the livestock sector value chain.
the adoption and diffusion of new technologies in smallholder livestock systems requires more than just technical knowledge.
